blocks.text: City of Langley Condos for Sale

parts.t: The City of Langley is a compact, walkable city of about 10 km², and most of its condos sit within a few blocks of Fraser Highway. From many buildings you can walk to groceries, coffee, the library and bus routes. The
Surrey Langley SkyTrain
is also planned, with its last stop east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue. Below are the current listings, with a short guide to the City after them.

blocks.text: Living in a City of Langley condo
Downtown and the Fraser Highway core

parts.t: Downtown Langley City runs along Fraser Highway and the streets around it, with Douglas Crescent and Glover Road close by. Condo buildings here range from older low-rise walk-ups to newer mid-rise buildings with underground parking. The pull is simple: you can do most errands on foot. There are restaurants and small shops, and Timms Community Centre at 20399 Douglas Crescent is joined to City Hall and the Fraser Valley Regional Library branch. It suits people who want to drive less, first-time buyers, and anyone who likes being close to the action.

blocks.text: Near the Nicomekl River and Douglas Park

parts.t: South of the core, buildings sit closer to green space. Douglas Park, at 206 Street and Douglas Crescent, has a playground, a seasonal spray park, pickleball courts and community gardens. The Nicomekl floodplain and the Rotary Floodplain Trail give you a long, flat walk right in town, with Portage Park at 204 Street and 51A Avenue as a main entrance. These blocks tend to be a bit quieter than Fraser Highway while staying a short walk from downtown. Some homes sit near the floodplain, so ask about flood mapping for the exact address. It suits dog owners, walkers, and downsizers who want trails and shops in the same walk.
The Province's
Surrey Langley SkyTrain project

extends the Expo Line 16 kilometres, mostly along Fraser Highway, from King George Station. Langley City Centre station is planned east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue, with a transit exchange. Willowbrook station, at the northeast corner of 196 Street and Fraser Highway, also gets an exchange and sits where Surrey, the City and the Township all meet. The Province says the trip from Langley City Centre to King George will take about 22 minutes, and service is expected in late 2029. It suits commuters heading west and buyers planning a few years ahead.

blocks.text: Things to check in older City buildings

parts.t: Many City condos are in older buildings. Before you write an offer, read the depreciation report and two years of strata minutes. Ask about the roof, windows, plumbing and any planned special levies. A good inspection is worth the cost.

I've helped buyers look at condos in downtown Langley City, and the older buildings here can be good value when the paperwork is in order. If you find one you like, I'm happy to go through the strata package with you line by line before you commit.

blocks.text: Where will the SkyTrain stop in the City of Langley?

parts.t: The last station, Langley City Centre, is planned east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue, with a transit exchange. Willowbrook station, at the northeast corner of 196 Street and Fraser Highway, is on the City's western edge, where it meets Surrey and the Township.

blocks.text: When will the Surrey Langley SkyTrain open?

parts.t: The Province of BC currently expects service to begin in late 2029. Dates can shift, so check
surreylangleyskytrain.gov.bc.ca
for updates.

blocks.text: Is the City of Langley the same as the Township of Langley?

parts.t: No. The City is a separate, smaller municipality, bordered by Surrey on the west and surrounded by the Township on the other sides. Taxes, bylaws and services come from different local governments.

blocks.text: Can I live car-light in a City of Langley condo?

parts.t: In many downtown buildings, yes. Groceries, shops, the library and bus routes are within walking distance. Some trips still need a car or bus until the SkyTrain opens.

blocks.text: Are there flood concerns near the Nicomekl River?

parts.t: Some areas near the river are in the floodplain. Ask for the City's flood mapping for the exact address, and check with your insurer before you remove subjects.
